narrative:
The model estimated your probability of bad credit at 41.0%. For this lending decision, that risk level was treated as too high, so your application was denied; it does not mean default is certain, only that the assessed risk exceeded the approval threshold.

The strongest factor behind the decision was the status of your checking account. Your account is in the negative range, and this pushed the assessment toward bad credit. That matters because approved applicants rarely show this status: most had no recorded checking-account balance, while only about 12.6% were in the negative group. The second strongest factor was your repayment instalments as a share of disposable income. At 2.00, below the approved average of 2.99, this counted in your favour by suggesting a lighter monthly burden. The third factor was the requested loan length. Your 12-month request is shorter than the approved average of 19.17 months, so it also counted in your favour. Those two favourable points helped, but they did not outweigh the checking-account concern.

Ask the lender what specific evidence would support a future application. The clearest next step is to bring your checking account into positive standing and keep it there. Continue keeping instalments modest, avoid adding new credit, and consider reapplying once your account status has improved; a smaller request or a guarantor may also strengthen a future application.
